message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance equipped with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
It covers both the `gcloud` CLI command (the quickest way) and the raw REST‑API payload (if you prefer to call the API directly).

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** must be enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You need the **GPU quota** for the zone you choose (e.g., `us-central1-a`).  
> * The **NVIDIA driver** will be installed automatically by the GPU‑enabled image.  

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI – One‑liner

```bash
# Replace PROJECT_ID, ZONE, INSTANCE_NAME with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
    --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
    --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
    --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
    --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
    --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
    --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: custom init script
    --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \
    --tags="http-server,https-server" \
    --labels="env=dev,gpu=true"
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `count=1` means one RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Uses the official Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | `TERMINATE` ensures the VM is stopped if the host is reclaimed. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts the VM if it crashes. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional shell script that runs at first boot (e.g., install CUDA). |
| `--scopes` | Grants full Cloud Platform access. |
| `--tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules. |
| `--labels` | Adds key/value metadata for filtering. |

> 📌 **Tip** – If you need more GPUs, just change `count=2` (or higher) and adjust the machine type accordingly (e.g., `n1-highmem-32`).

---

## 2️⃣  REST API – Full JSON Payload

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a CI/CD pipeline), use the following JSON body.  
Send it to the endpoint:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your values.

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "labels": {
    "env": "dev",
    "gpu": "true"
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y cuda-drivers\n"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Key points

| Field | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `machineType` | Must reference the full path (`zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/...`). |
| `guestAccelerators` | Specifies the GPU type and count. |
| `disks.initializeParams.sourceImage` | Uses the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS family. |
| `metadata.items[0].value` | Optional startup script (here installing CUDA drivers). |
| `scheduling.onHostMaintenance` | `TERMINATE` ensures graceful shutdown on host maintenance. |

> 🔧 **Authentication** – Use OAuth 2.0 with a scope of `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute`.  
> 🛠️ **Error handling** – If you hit a quota error, check the “GPU quota” section in the GCP console.

---

## 3️⃣  Quick sanity check

After launching, verify the instance:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --project=my-gcp-project \
    --zone=us-central1-a \
    --format="table(name, status, machineType, guestAccelerators[*].acceleratorType, guestAccelerators[*].acceleratorCount)"
```

You should see something like:

```
NAME                STATUS  MACHINE_TYPE                     GUEST_ACCELERATORS[*].ACCELERATOR_TYPE  GUEST_ACCELERATORS[*].ACCELERATOR_COUNT
rtx-a6000-ubuntu    RUNNING n1-standard-8                    nvidia-tesla-a6000                      1
```

---

## 4️⃣  Optional: Customizing the GPU driver

The default GPU‑enabled image installs the NVIDIA driver automatically.  
If you need a specific driver version or CUDA toolkit, add a `startup-script` that pulls the desired packages. Example:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install CUDA 12.1
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-ubuntu2004.pin
mv cuda-ubuntu2004.pin /etc/apt/preferences.d/cuda-repository-pin-600
add-apt-repository "deb http://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/ /"
apt-key adv --fetch-keys https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/7fa2af80.pub
apt-get update
apt-get -y install cuda-12-1
```

Add this script to the `metadata.items[0].value` field in the REST payload or pass it via `--metadata-from-file startup-script`.

---

### TL;DR

* **CLI**: `gcloud compute instances create ... --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1"`
* **REST**: POST to `/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances` with JSON above.  
* **Result**: A running VM with an RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  

Happy GPU computing! 🚀
